blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Automated ideation systems are often evaluated on the novelty of the ideas they produce, and that judgment is increasingly delegated to large language models. Such judges are typically built ad hoc and validated, if at all, on human-authored papers rather than on the generated ideas they are meant to score. So, how do novelty judges perform? Not well. We present a systematic controlled study of novelty evaluation design choices. We first build an evaluation set automatically, mining OpenReview for passages where reviewers explicitly affirm or dispute a paper’s originality and keeping only submissions with unanimous agreement at the extremes of their research area; we pair these with ideas from a vanilla LLM generator. Across six judges, we find that small prompt design choices have large consequences; e.g., simply telling the judge that reviewers found one idea novel and the other not can change its verdict on more than half of the identical idea pairs it is shown, shifting pairwise accuracy by over 50 points and occasionally pushing it below chance. The same change helps one judge and hurts another. Retrieval and larger reasoning budgets help little, and two purpose-built novelty evaluators are outperformed by our cheapest prompted baseline. These results raise questions about reported novelty gains of automated ideation systems, and call for robust novelty evaluation methods.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en: Recent years have seen a proliferation of systems that generate research ideas and propose new directions. A central criterion for judging such systems is novelty : whether the ideas they produce contribute a meaningful conceptual advance. Many works therefore automate this assessment, using it both to evaluate the ideas a system outputs and as an internal component of the ideation pipeline, letting agents filter and refine a pool of candidate ideas Wang et al. (2024) ; Yamada et al. (2025) .

Validation rests on small annotated sets Radensky et al. (2026) , outdated data that predates LLMs’ knowledge cutoffs Shen et al. (2026) , or human-authored papers Si et al. blocks.en: We present a systematic, extensive study of LLM-based novelty evaluation. Through controlled experiments, we vary different design choices practitioners make: which LLM is used as a judge and how the judge is prompted, whether evaluation is pointwise (is this idea novel?) or pairwise (which of these two is more novel?), its reasoning budget, whether it may retrieve related work, and the format of the judged ideas. We evaluate judges on human-authored ideas, and explore how their behavior changes when human-authored and LLM-generated ideas are judged together. Additionally, we benchmark off-the-shelf LLMs against specialized novelty judges Yamada et al. (2025) ; Shahid et al. (2025) .
blocks.zh: 我们对基于LLM的新型评价进行了系统而广泛的研究。 通过受控的实验,我们不同不同的设计选择 实践者: LLM是作为判断者使用的,以及判断者是如何被激发的,评价是指向的(这是这个思想新颖的吗?)还是双向的(这两个中哪一个是比较新颖的?),其推理预算,它是否可以检索相关的作品,以及判断思想的格式. 我们评价由人类提出的想法的评委,并探讨当由人类提出和由LLM产生的想法一起判断时,他们的行为如何改变. 此外,我们将现成的LLMs与专业新颖法官山田等人(2025年);Shahid等人(2025年)作为基准。

blocks.en: To enable our experiments, we construct a benchmark using an automated pipeline that mines high-precision novelty labels from peer reviews (Figure 2 ). Unlike prior work that relies on coarse proxies such as paper acceptance Qiao et al. (2026) or outdated novelty scores that venues no longer publish Schopf and Färber (2026) , we derive labels from the underlying review text. Specifically, we isolate passages where reviewers explicitly affirm or dispute the originality of a contribution, retaining only submissions with unanimous consensus that fall within the top or bottom decile of their venue. We complement these with LLM-generated ideas, sampled under settings that with high probability yield lower novelty than the top human-authored ideas.
blocks.zh: 为了使我们能够进行实验,我们用一个自动管道构建一个基准,从同行评审中开采高精度新标志(图2)。 与先前依赖粗糙的代理作品,如纸质接受Qiao等人(2026年)或过时的新颖评分,地点不再发布Schopf和Färber(2026年)不同,我们从基本的审查文本中衍生出标签. 具体地说,我们孤立了一些段落,其中审查人员明确确认或质疑某项贡献的原创性,只保留在会议地点的上下十级范围内的协商一致提交材料。 我们用LLM生成的理念来补充这些理念,这些理念在极有可能产生比人类最高作者的理念更低新颖的环境下进行采样.

blocks.en: Using this benchmark, we find that novelty judges are strikingly brittle. Small changes to the evaluation setup, such as telling the judge that reviewers found one of two ideas novel, change a judge’s verdict on more than half of the identical pairs it is shown and swing its accuracy by more than 50 points (Figure 1 ). Judges also behave differently on AI-generated ideas than on human-authored ones, exposing a systematic gap in current evaluation practice: pairwise judges degrade once the comparison involves generated ideas, and grow markedly more brittle there. No single fix helps across the board. Judges are calibrated differently from one another, and the techniques commonly reached for to improve them, such as reasoning effort and retrieval, have limited effect and can even degrade some models. We further show that the additional complexity and monetary investment in dedicated novelty-evaluation models do not necessarily translate to better novelty verdicts.

blocks.en: Our contributions are as follows:
blocks.zh: 我们的捐款如下:

blocks.en: • A systematic controlled study of novelty judges, spanning six judge backbones, pointwise and pairwise judgments, and common design choices such as prompt wording, retrieval, reasoning effort, and idea format. Additionally, we compare judge behavior on human-written and LLM-generated ideas. • An automated, reusable pipeline that mines explicit novelty signals from peer reviews to build novelty evaluation benchmarks. Using this pipeline, we construct two core evaluation setups: Human-Only (strongest high-novelty vs. weakest low-novelty human papers) and Human+Generated (strongest high-novelty vs. ideas from a deliberately simple LLM generator). The pipeline can be rerun on new conference data, and we release all data and code as an open resource. • An empirical finding that judge verdicts depend heavily on how the evaluation is configured: the same judge returns different verdicts on the same instances under different configurations. Spending more does not always buy better performance on this task.

blocks.en: 3 An Automated Pipeline for Creating Novelty Evaluation Benchmarks
blocks.zh: 3 创建新评价基准的自动化管道

blocks.en:
At a high level, our goal is to evaluate novelty judges in a range of different settings: ideas spanning higher and lower levels of novelty, authored both by humans and by automated ideation systems. We collect ideas and organize them into two conceptual pools, such that ideas in one are expected to be more novel than those in the other. These pools support both pointwise judgments of whether an individual idea is novel and pairwise judgments of which of two ideas is more novel.
This section describes how we automatically collect ideas and their corresponding novelty labels from multiple sources, and how we assemble them into our benchmark. Our collection pipeline is automated, allowing the benchmark to scale to larger idea pools. It is also reusable: it can be re-run on the reviews of future conference cycles, keeping the benchmark evergreen. Notably, our pipeline is not tied to ICLR: it applies to any venue that publishes free-text reviews, such as NeurIPS, which releases reviews for accepted papers and for rejected ones whose authors opt in, or ACL Rolling Review 1 1 1 https://arr-data.aclweb.org/resources/ . The automatic data collection process is depicted in Figure 2 .
blocks.zh:
在高级别上,我们的目标是在一系列不同的环境下评价新颖性法官:跨越新颖性的更高和更低层次的思想,这些思想由人类和自动化思想系统共同撰写。 我们收集各种想法,把它们组织成两个概念库,这样,预期一个想法比另一个想法更新颖。 这些集合既支持对个人思想是否是新颖的判断,又支持对两种思想中哪一种是新颖的判断。

blocks.en: 3.1 Labeled Ideas Collection

blocks.en: We extract novelty labels from ICLR 2026 2026 submissions and their corresponding reviews. While some prior work builds idea-assessment datasets from review data, it derives either no explicit quality labels Moussa et al. (2026) ; Wu et al. (2026) , or labels from coarse proxies such as acceptance decisions Qiao et al. (2026) . Such proxies fold additional quality dimensions into the verdict, and a paper can be accepted while its reviewers consider the contribution incremental. A third line relies on novelty scores that venues no longer publish Schopf and Färber (2026) , so the procedure cannot be re-run on newer submissions.
blocks.zh: 我们从ICLR 2026 2026号呈件及其相应的审查中提取新颖的标签. 虽然以前的一些工作从审查数据中构建了思想评估数据集,但它要么没有从Moussa等人(2026年);Wu等人(2026年)获得明确的质量标签,要么从粗糙的代名词,如接受决定Qiao等人(2026年)获得标签。 这种代理将额外的质量维度折叠到判决中,文件可以被接受,而其审查者则考虑贡献递增. 第三行依靠新颖的分数,地点不再发布Schopf和Färber(2026年),因此该程序无法在更新的提交书上重新运行.

blocks.en: Reviewers do state verdicts on originality, but in prose, scattered across the free-form strengths and weaknesses sections. We therefore derive our labels from the review text itself: we prompt claude-opus-4-6 to extract novelty signals , snippets of text where reviewers affirm or dispute the novelty of the contribution itself . Appendix A.1 lists the extraction prompt used and signal examples.
blocks.zh: 评论家对原创性做州级裁决,但以散文形式,分散在自由式优缺点科. 因此,我们从审查案文本身引出我们的标签:我们敦促Claude-opus-4-6提取新颖的信号,即审查者确认或质疑贡献本身新颖之处的案文片段。 附录A.1列出了所使用的提取提示和信号示例。

blocks.en: In our setting, an idea is deemed novel when its reviewers judge the contribution original and the submission sits at the top of the venue. The first is established by the novelty signals themselves: a majority of reviewers give a positive novelty signal, and no reviewer gives a negative one. The second is established by the review scores: the paper is accepted, its average rating falls in the top decile of its ICLR primary area, and its average contribution score clears a fixed floor. We treat each submission’s abstract as its idea.
blocks.zh: 在我们的环境下,当其审查者判断贡献的原创性,而呈文坐落在会场的顶端时,一个想法被认为是新的。 第一种由新颖的信号本身所建立:大多数审查者给出了正面的新颖信号,没有审查者给出了负面信号. 第二种由审查分数确定:论文被接受,其平均评分在ICLR主片区最高十分位下降,其平均贡献分数清出一个固定的下限. 我们把每个划界案的抽象概念视为其理念。

blocks.en: Table 1: Data setups statistics. D + D_{+} holds the novel ideas and D − D_{-} the lower-novelty ones. Both setups share D + D_{+} ( 154 154 ICLR-validated novel ideas) and differ in D − D_{-} : validated lower-novelty ICLR ideas in Human-Only , and LLM-generated ideas in Human+Generated .
blocks.zh: 表1:数据设置统计。 D + D + 持有新颖的创意和 D → D → → ) 低新颖的创意. 两种设置都共享D+D_{+}(154 154 ICLR-验证小说思想),在D−D_{-}中存在差异:在Human-Only中验证了低新颖的ICLR思想,在Human+Generated中验证了LLM产生的思想.

blocks.en: The complementary pool inverts every criterion. Its reviewers must flag issues with the contribution’s originality: a majority give negative novelty signals, and no reviewer gives a positive one. Its submission must sit at the bottom of the venue: rejected, with an average rating in the bottom decile of its ICLR primary area and an average contribution score below a fixed ceiling. Appendix A.1 lists additional details on mining novelty labels from human reviews.
blocks.zh: 互补池颠倒了每个标准。 其审查者必须用贡献的原创性标出问题:多数人给出了负面的新颖信号,没有审查者给出正面信号。 它的呈文必须坐落在会场底部:被拒绝,在ICLR主区底部的十分级中平均评分,平均贡献分低于固定上限. 附录A.1列出了从人类评论中获得的关于采矿新颖性标签的其他细节.

blocks.en: Figure 3: Study overview. We cross two judgment formats with six judge backbones and six evaluation dimensions. We run one configuration at a time and report the results on both data setups, Human-Only and Human+Generated .
blocks.zh: 图3:研究概览。 我们跨越两个判决格式,有六个法官骨干和六个评价层面。 我们一次运行一个配置 并报告两个数据组合的结果, 仅人类和人类+基因。

blocks.en:
Work that evaluates novelty judges at scale does so exclusively on human-authored papers Schopf and Färber (2026) ; Moussa et al. (2026) , rather than on the machine-generated ideas that are the target distribution when evaluating ideation systems. Conversely, work that does examine generated ideas relies on expert annotation Si et al. (2024) ; Shahid et al. (2025) and is consequently small (tens of ideas). Such annotations are slow and expensive to collect, and, once released, liable to leak into the training data of the very models later used as novelty judges.
Worse, these expert labels are themselves unstable, as shown by Si et al. (2025) , where the scores of LLM-generated ideas, including their novelty scores, dropped significantly once the ideas were executed and reviewed again.
blocks.zh:
大规模评价新颖法官的工作完全依靠人类撰写的论文Schopf和Färber(2026年);Moussa等人(2026年),而不是在评价思想系统时作为目标分布的机器产生的思想。 相反,研究所产生想法的工作依赖于专家注释Si等人(2024年);Shahid等人(2025年),因此规模较小(十种想法)。 这种说明很慢,收集费用昂贵,一旦公布,就有可能泄露到后来作为新颖法官使用的模型的培训数据中。
更糟糕的是,这些专家标签本身是不稳定的,如Si等人(2025年)所显示的,LLM产生的想法的分数,包括其新颖的分数,一旦这些想法被执行并再次审查,就会大幅下降.

blocks.en:
We therefore build the generated pool under an explicit weak-labeling assumption: every idea in the generated pool is less novel than every validated novel idea . We design the pool to keep this assumption conservative. Its human side is the validated novel pool described above: top-decile accepted ICLR papers whose reviewers, having read the full paper, unanimously affirmed the novelty of the contribution. Its generated side comes from claude-sonnet-4-5 , a deliberately non-frontier model released over a year ago, which is given only the ICLR primary area of its human counterpart and asked to ‘‘generate a novel idea’’ in a single pass, with no literature access, tools, scaffold, or feedback.
We argue this is highly plausible given the state of technology in 2025 2 2 2 See discussion on using newer models in Appendix C.2.1 . .
blocks.zh:
因此,我们用一个明显的微弱标签假设来建造生成的池:生成的池中的每一个想法都不如每一个经过验证的新想法新颖。 我们设计游泳池是为了保守这种假设。 它的人性方面是上面描述的经过验证的小说集合:顶级十进制被接受的ICLR论文,其审查者在阅读了整篇论文后,一致肯定了该贡献的新颖性. 它生成的侧面来自Claude-sonnet-4-5,这是一年多前发行的刻意非边际模型,它只被赋予其人类对应物的ICLR主要领域,并要求‘‘在单传中生成一个新思想’’,没有文献访问,工具,脚手架或反馈.
我们认为,鉴于2025年的技术状况,这一点非常合理。

blocks.en:
As a check that the assumption is not obviously violated, a computer science professor with broad expertise across AI areas
judged 30 pairs from Human+Generated blind to source and with idea order shuffled, giving written justifications and citing prior work where relevant. To stress the assumption where it is most likely to fail, 28 of the pairs were ones our strongest pairwise judge ( claude-opus-4-6 ) got wrong under the reference configuration, and two were controls it got right. The expert sided with the human idea in all 30 pairs, with no ties, over roughly five hours of annotation. We present this as a sanity check on the hardest cases rather than a validation of every label (see Appendix A.3 for details and examples). We also normalize the style of human and generated ideas to evaluate potential judge shortcuts (Section 5 ).
blocks.zh:
作为这一假设没有被明显违反的一种检查,一位具有广泛专业知识的计算机科学教授跨AI领域
判断30对来自Human+Generated的盲从源头,并按思想顺序洗牌,给出书面理由,并酌情引用先前的工作。 为了强调它最有可能失败的假设,28对夫妇是我们最强的对偶裁判(claude-opus-4-6)在参考配置下出错,两对是控制它得到正确. 专家在所有30对中支持人类思想,没有关系,大约5小时的注释. 我们提出这是对最困难情况的一种理智检查,而不是对每个标签的验证(详情和例子见附录A.3)。 我们还使人文风格正常化,并产生一些想法来评价潜在的法官捷径(第5节)。

blocks.en: Finally, this labeling assumption has no bearing on our evaluation of instability : two configurations that return different verdicts on the same pair cannot both be right, whatever its label.
blocks.zh: 最后,这个标签的假设与我们对不稳定性的评价无关 : 两种配置,

blocks.en: 3.2 Benchmark Construction
blocks.zh: 3.2 基准建设

blocks.en: We consider the two forms of novelty evaluation in common use: (1) Pointwise Shahid et al. (2025) ; Yamada et al. (2025) , where the judge is given a single idea and decides whether or not it is novel (binary classification), and (2) Pairwise Qiao et al. (2026) , where the judge is given two ideas and decides which of the two is more novel (ranking). Beyond their prevalence, pointwise and pairwise evaluations are the atomic components underlying more complex assessment protocols, such as majority voting and tournament-style ranking Si et al. (2024) ; Gottweis et al. (2025) .
blocks.zh: 我们认为两种形式的新颖评价是常用的:(1)Pointwise Shahid等人(2025年);山田等人(2025年),其中法官被赋予一个单一的想法,并决定是否是新颖的(二进制分类),(2)Pairwise Qiao等人(2026年),其中法官被赋予两个想法,并决定其中哪一种是比较新颖的(等级). 除了其普遍程度之外,指针式和对针式的评价是更复杂的评估协议所依据的原子成分,如多数投票和联赛式排名Si等人(2024年);Gottweis等人(2025年)。

blocks.en: We assemble the collected ideas into two setups, each a pair of pools: 𝑫 + \boldsymbol{D_{+}} ( novel ideas ), and 𝑫 − \boldsymbol{D_{-}} (l ower-novelty ideas ), populated so that an idea drawn from D + D_{+} can be assumed more novel than one drawn from D − D_{-} . In Human-Only , D + D_{+} holds the validated novel ideas and D − D_{-} the validated lower-novelty ideas, so both sides are human-authored. In Human+Generated , D + D_{+} is unchanged and D − D_{-} holds the weakly labeled generated ideas. The two setups thus share D + D_{+} and differ only in the source of D − D_{-} . Accordingly, D − D_{-} does not denote a fixed set of ideas, but whichever pool fills the lower-novelty side of the setup at hand.
blocks.zh: 我们把收集到的想法组合成两组,每组一对池: D +\boldsymbol{D_{+}}(小说思想),D →\boldsymbol{D_{(l ower-novelty思想),人口众多,因此从D + 中引出一个想法. DQQ可以假定比D~DQQ} 所引的更新颖. 在"人类独行"中,D+DQQ持有经过验证的小说思想,而D+DQQ)则持有经过验证的低新颖思想,因此双方都是人类著作. 在Human+Generated中,D+D+QQ没有改变,D−D+Q}持有被贴上弱标签的生成思想. 这两个设置因此共享D+D+QQ,仅在D−D+Q}的来源上有所不同. 因此,D − D → } 不表示一套固定的想法,但无论哪个池子都充斥着手头的下层新颖面.

blocks.en: Each data setup supports both pointwise and pairwise judgment, and both draw on both pools. In pointwise , every idea in either pool is one instance, labeled by its pool: ideas in D + D_{+} are labeled novel and ideas in D − D_{-} not novel . In pairwise , each idea in D + D_{+} is matched with one from D − D_{-} in the same ICLR primary area (e.g., generative models ), so the two sides are topically comparable. In Human-Only , where D − D_{-} is the smaller pool, an idea may be matched more than once. Table 1 reports the resulting statistics.
blocks.zh: 每个数据设置都支持对准和对偶的判断,两者都借鉴两个集合. D+D+QQ的想法被标注为小说, 成对地,D+D+QQ中的每个想法都与来自同一ICLR主区域(如基因模型)的D−D+QQ−)的每个想法相匹配,因此双方在主题上是可比较的. 在"人类之独"(Human-Only)中,D-D_{-(D_{)是较小的游泳池,一个想法可能不止一次匹配. 表1报告了由此产生的统计数据。

blocks.en: An idea in our benchmark is a single abstract, human-authored or generated. A submission’s own abstract advertises experimental outcomes that an LLM ideator, with no execution, cannot produce without hallucinating results. We therefore apply claude-opus-4-6 to every human abstract to remove evaluation artifacts (e.g., numerical results, claims of superiority to specific baselines). Prompt 2 in Appendix A.1 presents the full instructions for this step. Generated ideas are emitted in this same format and need no such treatment.
blocks.zh: 在我们的基准中,一个想法是一个单一的抽象的,由人类创造或产生的. 呈文本身的抽象宣传实验结果,一个LLM思想家,没有执行,没有幻觉结果就无法产生. 因此,我们对每一个人类抽象体都应用claude-opus-4-6来去除评价文物(例如,数字结果,声称优于特定基线). 附录A.1中的提示2为这一步骤提供了全部说明。 所产生的想法都以同样的形式提出,不需要这种处理。

blocks.en: 4 Experimental Setup
blocks.zh: 4 实验设置

blocks.en: Table 2: Controlled changes. Each change modifies a single design choice relative to the reference configuration, holding the rest of the novelty evaluation process fixed. Columns mark the protocols (Pt: pointwise, Pw: pairwise) and data setups (HO: Human-Only , HG: Human+Generated ) each change is run under. Beyond these single changes, we compare prompted judges to dedicated novelty judges (Fig. 6 ) and to a strong agentic RAG judge (Fig. 5 ).
blocks.zh: 表2:受控制的变化。 每次修改都会对参考配置进行单一的设计选择,将新颖评价过程的其余部分固定下来. 列标记协议(Pt:pointwise,Pw:pairwise)和数据设置(HO:Human-Only,HG:Human+Generated),每个更改都在下面运行. 除了这些单一的变化之外,我们比较了促使法官们敬业的新颖法官(图6)和一位强有力的代理法官(图5)。

blocks.en: We perform a systematic study of novelty judges, spanning both judgment formats, a range of judge backbones, and several evaluation dimensions, on both data setups (Figure 3 ). Each run modifies a single design choice relative to a reference configuration , holding the rest of the evaluation process fixed. Table 2 summarizes the reference and the controlled changes we apply to it. Additional implementation details are in Appendix C.1 .
blocks.zh: 我们系统地研究新颖的法官,既包括判决格式,也包括法官的骨干,也包括两个数据集的若干评价层面(图3)。 每次运行都会相对于参考配置修改单一的设计选择,将其余的评价过程固定下来. 表2汇总了参考文献和我们对其适用的可控制的改动。 其他执行情况详见附录C.1。

blocks.en: 4.1 Reference Configuration
blocks.zh: 4.1 参考配置

blocks.en: Given a single idea (pointwise) or a pair of ideas (pairwise), we ask the judge to return a novelty verdict together with the reasoning behind it. Judges are prompted with reasoning_effort = high (when they expose this parameter) and with no access to literature search.
blocks.zh: 考虑到一个单一的想法(意见)或一对想法(意见),我们要求法官将一个新颖的判决连同其背后的推理一起退回。 法官受到推理(effort)=高(当他们披露这一参数时)的激励,无法查阅文献。

blocks.en: To improve prediction stability, we aggregate multiple verdicts from the judge. In the pointwise case we take the majority vote of three calls. In the pairwise case we call the judge three times per presentation order ( A A vs. B B and B B vs. A A ) to mitigate position bias ( Wang et al., 2023 ) . We score each idea by the fraction of the six calls that select it and award the comparison to the idea with the higher score. When the two ideas receive equal scores, we record a tie , i.e., the judge is unable to distinguish between them. The exact reference prompts and implementation details are given in Appendix B.1 .
blocks.zh: 为了提高预测稳定性,我们汇集了法官的多项判决。 在这种情况下,我们以三通电话的多数票表决。 在对等的案件中,我们每次向法官发出三次陈述令(A诉B和B诉A),以减轻职位偏差(Wang等人,2023年)。 我们通过选择它的六个电话的一小部分来评分每个想法,并以更高的分数来评分与这个想法的比较. 当两个想法得到相等分数时,我们记录一个平局,即裁判无法区分它们. 确切的参考提示和执行细节见附录B.1。

blocks.en: Both data setups share the same D + D_{+} , the 154 154 validated novel ICLR ideas, and differ only in D − D_{-} (Section 3.2 , Table 1 ). In Human-Only , D − D_{-} holds the validated lower-novelty ICLR ideas. In Human+Generated , D − D_{-} is populated by a non-SOTA model ( claude-sonnet-4-5 ) prompted to “generate an idea” with no scaffold, literature access, or tools (Section 3.1 ). Since the generator fixes the low-novelty side of the benchmark, we also treat it as one of the controllable parameters in the study.
blocks.zh: 两个数据集共用相同的D+D_{+},154个经验证的ICLR小说理念,仅D−D_{-}不同. (第3.2节,表1) 在"唯人"(Human-Only)中,D − D → }持有经过验证的低新颖ICLR思想. 在Human+Generated 中,D − D − } 由非SOTA模型(claude-sonnet-4-5)所居住,该模型旨在“生成一个想法”,没有脚手架、文献访问或工具(第3.1节)。 由于生成器修补了基准的低新星一侧,我们也把它当作研究中的可控参数之一.

blocks.en: 4.2 Explored Evaluation Dimensions
blocks.zh: 4.2 探讨的评价方面

blocks.en: The instructions given to the judge. We explore six variants: the reference prompt and five modifications (P1–P5, specified in Table 2 ). P1 and P2 weaken the novelty definition given in the reference prompt: P1 drops the instruction that warns against trivial or incremental contributions, and P2 removes the definition of novelty altogether. P3–P5 (a family of pairwise prompts inspired by Si et al. (2024) ) simply ask the judge to choose between two ideas, differing only in small changes: P3 tells the judge that reviewers at a top AI conference found one idea novel and the other not, P4 omits this reviewer framing and directly asks which idea is novel, and P5 retains the reviewer framing but asks which idea was judged more novel.
blocks.zh: 给法官的指示。 我们探讨六个变体:参考即时和五个修改(表2具体说明的P1-P5)。 P1和P2削弱了引用提示中给出的新颖性定义:P1放弃了警告小贡献或增量贡献的指令,P2完全取消了新颖性的定义. P3–P5(由Si等人(2024年)所启发的对等提示家族)只是要求法官在两个想法之间做出选择,只在小的改变中有所区别: P3告诉法官,在一次AI顶级大会上,审查者发现一个想法小说,而另一个没有,P4省略了这个审查者设定,直接询问哪个想法是新颖的,P5保留了审查者设定,但询问哪个想法被评为更新颖的.

blocks.en: P3–P5 introduce small, local changes to the instructions: whether the judgment is framed through prior peer review and whether novelty is expressed in binary or comparative terms. Will these choices affect how the judge interprets novelty? Our question is how strongly the resulting evaluations depend on such seemingly minor prompt-design decisions, which practitioners must make when constructing a novelty judge. These prompts are not semantically identical; nevertheless, each asks the judge to select between the same two ideas on the basis of novelty. They represent closely related formulations that a practitioner could reasonably consider when implementing the same evaluation goal (indeed, the prompts closely follow Si et al. (2024) ). Some variation in judgments is therefore unsurprising; our question is how large that variation becomes. We find that these local changes can produce substantially different verdicts and performance estimates, particularly when evaluating generated ideas.
blocks.zh: P3–P5对指令引入了小的,局部的修改:判断是否通过事先的同行评审来设定,以及新颖性是用二进制还是比较式表达. 这些选择会影响法官对新事物的解释吗? 我们的问题是,所产生的评价在多大程度上依赖于这种看来微不足道的迅速设计决定,而实践者在组建新法官时必须作出这种决定。 这些提示并非完全相同;不过,每个提示都要求法官根据新颖性在相同的两个想法中作出选择。 它们代表了从业人员在执行同一评价目标时可以合理考虑的密切相关的表述(事实上,提示紧跟Si等人(2024年))。 因此,判决中的某些变化并不令人惊奇;我们的问题是,这种变化有多大。 我们认为,这些地方变化可以产生大不相同的判断和业绩估计,特别是在评价所产生的想法时。

blocks.en: Whether the judge sees related work alongside the idea. In the retrieval condition the judge additionally receives 5 5 abstracts of related work, collected with a Paper-Finder 3 3 3 https://github.com/allenai/asta-paper-finder pipeline: we first isolate the contributions of the judged idea, then generate 5 5 targeted queries that probe the novelty of those contributions, and finally keep, for each query, the most relevant paper published before a fixed retrieval cutoff (2025-03-01). The cutoff sits about six months before the ICLR 2026 abstract deadline (2025-09-19). Authors often post drafts to arXiv well before submitting, and this margin keeps such preprints, which would reveal the very idea under evaluation, out of the retrieved work. We also adjust the prompt accordingly, asking the judge to assess novelty with respect to the retrieved work.
blocks.zh: 法官是否认为相关工作与想法并存. 在检索条件方面,法官另外收到5份相关工作摘要,这些摘要用Paper-Finder 3 3 https://github.com/allenai/asta-paper-finder管道收集:我们首先孤立已判断思想的贡献,然后产生5份有针对性的查询,调查这些贡献的新颖之处,最后为每个查询保留固定检索截止日期(2025-03-01)之前发表的最相关的论文。 截断时间大约在ICLR 2026抽象截止日期(2025-09-19)前6个月. 作者往往在提交草案之前就把草稿寄给arXiv,而这种差值保留了这类预印件,这些预印件将揭示所评价的理念,从所检索的作品中解脱出来. 我们还相应调整了提示,要求法官对收回的工作作出新颖的评估。

blocks.en: The inference-time reasoning budget given to the judge. Assessing novelty requires comparing an idea against the judge’s knowledge and deciding whether the overlap with prior work is substantial, which we expect to be reasoning-intensive. We test that expectation by lowering reasoning_effort from high to low for the backbones that expose the parameter.
blocks.zh: 给法官的推理预算。 评估新颖性需要将一个想法与法官的知识进行比较,并决定是否与以前的工作重叠很大,我们期望这是推理密集型的。 我们测试这种期望,将显示参数的骨干推理-努力从高降至低。

blocks.en: The surface form in which ideas are presented to the judge. Prior work presents ideas in different formats, from free-form abstracts Wang et al. (2024) to structured research plans Shahid et al. (2025) ; Si et al. (2024) , typically without justifying the choice. We therefore test the effect of converting every idea into a two-field purpose / mechanism plan, which holds the content of the idea fixed and changes only its presentation.
blocks.zh: 向法官介绍想法的表面形式。 以往的工作以不同格式从自由格式摘要中介绍各种想法 Wang等人(2024年)到结构化研究计划Shahid等人(2025年);Si等人(2024年),通常没有说明选择的理由. 因此,我们检验将每一种想法转变为一个双领域目的/机制计划的效果,该计划使想法的内容固定下来,只改变其表述方式。

blocks.en: The number of judge calls we pool into a single decision. Aggregation is a simple but costly way to stabilize verdicts Wang et al. (2023) . We test whether dividing the number of aggregated calls by 3 3 (calling pointwise judges once, pairwise judges once per presentation order) degrades the judges.
blocks.zh: 法官的数量要求我们做出一个判决 聚合是稳定王等人判决(2023年)的简单而昂贵的方法. 我们检验把总电话数除以3 3(一次点名法官,一次点名法官,一次点名法官)是否使法官退化。

blocks.en: The ideation model that produces the lower-novelty pool. We hold D + D_{+} fixed and regenerate D − D_{-} with three further backbones ( claude-opus-4-5 , gpt-5.1 , gpt-5.4 ), covering a weaker and a stronger model from each of two vendors.
blocks.zh: 产生低矮小池的构思模型. 我们持有D + D + 固定和再生 D → D → + + + + + + 加上另外三个骨干(claude-opus-4-5,gpt-5.1,gpt-5.4),覆盖两个供应商各自一个较弱和较强的模型.

blocks.en:
We run our controlled study with a range of judge backbone models ( gpt-5.{1,2,4} , claude-sonnet-4-5 , claude-opus-4-{5,6} ), all with training cutoffs predating the ICLR 2026 submission deadline so that the evaluated ideas fall outside their training data.
The novelty labels are further still out of reach: they are derived from reviews that were only released on OpenReview on 2025-11-12, roughly two months after the deadline. Thus, even if an idea reached a judge’s training data through an earlier preprint, the reviewers’ verdict on its novelty could not have.
blocks.zh:
我们用一系列的裁判骨干模型(gpt-5.{1,2,4},claude-sonnet-4-5,claude-opus-4-{5,6})来进行我们的控制下的研究,所有这些模型的训练截断时间都早于ICLR 2026提交截止日期,这样被评价的想法就超出了他们的训练数据.
这些新颖的标签还远未达到:它们来源于2025-11-12年才在公开评论上发布的评论,大约比截止日期晚了两个月。 因此,即使一个想法通过更早的预印获得法官的培训数据,审查者不可能对其新颖性做出判决。

blocks.en: 4.3 Dedicated Novelty Judges
blocks.zh: 4.3 专职小说法官

blocks.en: Our study focuses on prompted novelty judges: off-the-shelf LLMs instructed to return a novelty verdict. This is the setting in which novelty is assessed in most ideation systems Li et al. (2024) ; Hu et al. (2024) ; Shen et al. (2026) . However, we also perform a focused comparison with the more complex evaluation pipelines presented in prior work. Specifically, we examine two such judges. The first is Idea Novelty Checker Shahid et al. (2025) : a literature-grounded pipeline that retrieves a broad candidate pool by keyword search, narrows it through embedding-based filtering and LLM re-ranking, and assesses novelty against the surviving papers, guided by expert-labeled examples. The second is AI-Scientist Yamada et al. (2025) : a ReAct-style agent with Semantic Scholar access. The agent operates in a loop, where on each iteration it issues a search query, retrieves papers, and either decides on the idea’s novelty based on the results or continues searching.
blocks.zh: 我们的研究重点是激励新颖的法官:现成的LLMS指示退回一个新颖的判决. 这是在大多数思想体系中评估新颖性的背景:Li等人(2024年);Hu等人(2024年); 沈等 (2026) (中文(简体) ). 然而,我们还对先前工作中提出的更为复杂的评价程序进行了有重点的比较。 具体来说,我们审查了两名这样的法官。 第一种是Idea Novelty Checker Shahid et al. (2025):一个基于文献的管道,通过关键词搜索检索到一个广泛的候选集合,通过嵌入式过滤和LLM重排来缩小其范围,并以专家标记的例子为指南,对照幸存的论文评估新颖性. 其二是AI-科学家山田等人(2025年):具有语义学者访问权限的ReAct式代理. 代理商在一个循环中运作,每次迭代都发布搜索查询,检索文件,或者根据结果决定想法的新意,或者继续搜索.

blocks.en: 4.4 Evaluation Metrics
blocks.zh: 4.4 评价计量

blocks.en: For pointwise evaluation we report F1 per class (novel / not-novel) and a macro average. For pairwise, we report two versions of accuracy, differing in how they treat ties: (1) soft-accuracy : ties receive a credit of 0.5 0.5 ; (2) strict-accuracy : ties receive no credit at all.
blocks.zh: 为了进行点评,我们报告F1(小行星/非小行星)和宏观平均值。 就对等而言,我们报告两个版本的准确性,它们处理联系的方式各不相同:(1) 软准确性:联系获得0.5的信用;(2) 严格准确性:关系完全得不到任何信用。

blocks.en: We assess statistical significance with a two-sided paired non-parametric bootstrap ( 100,000 100{,}000 resamples) over the per-metric difference between each change and the reference configuration, using BCa 95 95 % confidence intervals. * marks differences whose 95 95 % CI excludes 0 0 (i.e., p < 0.05 p<0.05 ).
blocks.zh: 我们利用 BCa 95 95% 的置信间隔,评估每个变化与参考配置的每度测量差的统计意义,并使用双侧对齐的非参数靴子(10万100{,}000 复标). * 表示差异,95 95% CI不包括0(即p < 0.05 p < 0.05)。

blocks.en: (a) Pointwise judging, macro-F1.
blocks.zh: (a) 正确判断,宏观F1。

blocks.en: (b) Pairwise judging, strict-accuracy (ties count as failures).
blocks.zh: (b) 公平判断,严格准确(数十人算作失败)。

blocks.en: Figure 4: Cells report the change from the reference configuration, with the absolute value in parentheses. claude-sonnet-4-5 exposes no reasoning_effort parameter, hence the blank entry. Judges are highly unstable under even minor configuration changes, with large variance between models.
blocks.zh: 图4:单元格报告参考配置的变动,括号内为绝对值. Claude-sonnet-4-5没有显示推理_effort参数,因此是空白条目. 法官在甚至小的配置变化下都极不稳定,模型间差异很大.

blocks.en: 5 Results
blocks.zh: 5 结果

blocks.en: Figure 4 reports the ablation results for both pointwise (Figure 4(a) ) and pairwise (Figure 4(b) ) judgments. The first thing to note is that judges generally underperform, and rarely approach perfect results on this task. This happens even in the Human-Only setting, where D + D_{+} and D − D_{-} are drawn from opposite ends of the ICLR rating distribution and should be maximally separable.
blocks.zh: 图4分别报告了点(图4(a))和对点(图4(b))的判断结果。 需要注意的第一件事是,法官一般表现不佳,很少对这项任务取得圆满成果。 即使在人类独占的场合也会出现这种情况,D+D+和D−D+-)从ICLR评分分布的两端抽取,应当最大程度的分离.

blocks.en: Performance is also highly unstable under configuration changes. For instance, removing the guardrails from the novelty definition, or dropping the definition from the prompt entirely (P1–P2), generally degrades pairwise judges while helping some pointwise ones. On pairwise Human+Generated , replacing the reference prompt with one that asks which idea human reviewers judged as novel (P3) improves every judge (by more than 20 points in some cases). Yet a variant of that same prompt (P4), asking which idea is novel without referring to any prior human judgment, makes gpt-5.4 collapse below chance level. Because both prompts judge the same pairs, the 52.6-point gap between P3 and P4 means the two prompts return different verdicts on at least 52.6% of the pairs; whichever prompt is right on a pair, the other is wrong, so this instability does not depend on our labels.
blocks.zh: 在配置变化下性能也非常不稳定. 例如,从新定义中去掉护栏,或者将定义完全从即时(P1-P2)中去掉,一般会使双向裁判退化,同时帮助一些指针裁判。 在对称的Human+Generated(Human+Generated)上,将引用提示替换为询问被评为新奇(P3)的人类评论员认为哪一个理念可以改善每个评委(在某些情况下会提高20分以上). 然而,同一提示的变体(P4)询问哪个想法是新颖的,而没有提及任何先前的人类判断,使得gpt-5.4崩溃低于机会水平。 因为两个提示都判断同一对,所以P3和P4之间的52.6点差距意味着两个提示至少对52.6%的对对对返回不同的判定;无论哪个对对对对,另一个错,所以这种不稳定性并不取决于我们的标签.

blocks.en: To rule out the possibility that judges are reacting to stylistic differences between human-written and LLM-generated ideas rather than to their novelty, we rewrite all ideas into a shared plan format and rerun a subset of the changes that produced the largest shifts. The direction of the shifts is unchanged, and instability even grows: some changes flip the verdicts on more than two thirds of the examples (Figure 12 , Appendix C.2 ).
blocks.zh: 为了排除法官们对人文和LLM产生的想法之间的风格差异作出反应而不是对其新颖性作出反应的可能性,我们把所有的想法改写成一个共同的计划格式,重新运行产生最大转变的一组变化. 转向的方向没有改变,不稳定性甚至增加:有些变化推翻了三分之二以上的例子的判决(图12,附录C.2).

blocks.en: These shifts also do not move models together. The same change might be neutral or even beneficial for one judge, but destructive for another. This is seen most clearly in pointwise judging (e.g., P1–P2), but also in pairwise judgments: retrieval is a large gain for claude-opus-4-5 on Human+Generated while neutral for others. A configuration validated on one judge therefore carries no guarantee for the next.
blocks.zh: 这些转变也并不同时移动模型. 同样的变化可能中立,甚至有利于一名法官,但不利于另一名法官。 这一点在判断(如P1-P2)和对判(如P1-P2)中最明显地被看到:检索是Claude-opus-4-5在Human+Generated上的巨大收益,而对于其他人来说则是中性的。 因此,在一名法官身上验证的配置无法保证下一任法官。

blocks.en: We notice that design choices prior work commonly reaches for, like increased reasoning Saha et al. (2025) or retrieval Shahid et al. (2025) ; Lin et al. (2024) , have a limited and unexpected effect. Lowering the reasoning effort from "high" to "low" costs at most 7 7 performance points, and is usually neutral. Surprisingly, some models even benefit from using a smaller reasoning budget. Retrieval is similarly underwhelming: it induces a statistically significant improvement of at most 16 16 points (less than replacing the reference prompt with P3), only for some models, and never brings the absolute numbers near 100 100 . This remains true when D − D_{-} is generated by other ideation backbones, where retrieval even significantly degrades performance in some cases (Figure 14 ).
blocks.zh: 我们注意到,以前的工作通常会得到一些设计选择,例如增加Saha等人(2025年)或检索Shahid等人(2025年);Lin等人(2024年),但效果有限且出乎意料。 将推理工作从"高"降低到"低"成本,最多为7个7个性能点,通常为中性. 令人惊讶的是,一些模型甚至从使用较小的推理预算中受益. 检索同样是不足的:它导致统计学上在最多16个点(少于用P3取代引用提示)上的显著改进,仅对某些模型而言,绝对数字从未达到100 100。 当D − D − } 由其他想法主干线生成时,情况依然如此,在某些情况下,检索甚至显著降低性能(图14)。

blocks.en: The effect of the same prompt change also depends strongly on the evaluated data. For gpt-5.4 , switching from P3 to P4 changes strict accuracy by approximately 7 points on Human-Only , compared with 52.6 points on Human+Generated . Thus, a prompt choice that appears relatively benign when validating on human-authored ideas can have much larger consequences when the judge evaluates generated ideas, highlighting the importance of validation on the intended distribution.
blocks.zh: 同样迅速变化的效果也在很大程度上取决于评估的数据。 gpt-5.4,从P3切换到P4,在Human-Only的严格精度变化了约7分,而Human+Generated的精度为52.6分. 因此,当法官评价产生的想法时,在验证由人类提出的想法时,迅速作出的选择显得相对温和,会产生更大的后果,这突出了验证对预期分布的重要性。

blocks.en: Interestingly, removing instructions against trivial or additive novelty from the prompt (P1) harms every judge once AI-generated ideas are involved, while being mostly neutral on human-authored pairs. This might indicate that LLM-generated ideas lean more towards this style of ideation.
blocks.zh: 有趣的是,从即时(P1)中移除针对琐碎或添加性新颖性的指令,一旦涉及AI生成的想法,就会伤害每个法官,同时在人类作者的配对上大多保持中立. 这可能表明LLM产生的想法更倾向于这种思想风格.

blocks.en: We also vary the ideation model that generates D − D_{-} , and find that judges generally degrade once the lower-novelty ideas are LLM-generated rather than human-authored, with pairwise accuracy falling below chance against some backbones (Figure 13 , Appendix C.2.1 ).
blocks.zh: 我们还改变了产生D − D − } 的构思模型,发现一旦低新颖思想是LLM生成的,而不是由人类撰写的,而双向准确性低于某些骨干的机会(图13,附录C.2.1)。

blocks.en: Another disturbing pattern we observe is judge tie rates: how often a pairwise judge gives an uncertain novelty verdict (see Section 4.1 ). Depending on the configuration, even relatively strong judges like claude-opus-4-6 can tie on 35 % 35\% of the pairs, and weaker ones like claude-sonnet-4-5 on more than half . Correspondingly, ignoring ties or counting them as half-correct can substantially change how different evaluation systems are ranked (see soft-accuracy results in Figure 8 , Appendix C.2 ). Judges tie more often on Human+Generated than on Human-Only , roughly twice as often for claude-opus-4-5 and claude-sonnet-4-5 . This indicates higher uncertainty on this type of data. Turning off verdict aggregation contributes further uncertain predictions, and more than doubles tie rates in certain cases (Table 6 , Appendix C.2 ). This, together with the tendency to tie more on generated data, explains the performance drop this change introduces on Human+Generated .
blocks.zh: 我们观察到的另一个令人不安的模式是法官的平分率:双向法官常常作出不确定的新判决(见第4.1节)。 根据配置不同,即使Claude-opus-4-6等相对强大的评委也能在35%的35QQ对上打平,而较弱的评委则在超过一半的Claude-sonnet-4-5对上打平. 与此相对应,忽略联系或把它们算作半正确可以大大改变不同评价系统的排名(见图8,附录C.2.软准确性结果)。 法官们在Human+Generated上比在Human-Only上要多, 大约是Claude-opus-4-5和Claude-sonnet-4-5的两倍。 这表明这类数据的不确定性较高。 关闭判决汇总导致进一步的不确定预测,在某些情况下,双倍以上是平比率(表6,附录C.2)。 再加上在生成的数据上增加联系的倾向,

blocks.en: Finally, we observe that, in line with prior work Raina et al. (2024) ; Liusie et al. (2024) , pairwise judging is generally more stable than pointwise judging (especially with the Human-Only data). Appendix C.2 presents results for additional performance metrics, including results without verdict aggregation and our tie-rate analysis.
blocks.zh: 最后,我们观察到,根据先前的著作Raina等人(2024年);Liusie等人(2024年),对偶判断一般比对偶判断更为稳定(尤其是与仅人的数据相比)。 附录C.2列出了额外业绩衡量标准的结果,包括没有判断结果汇总的结果和我们的比对率分析。

blocks.en: 5.1 Retrieval’s Limitations
blocks.zh: 5.1 检索限制

blocks.en: Surprisingly, retrieval contributes limited performance gains, if at all (Figure 4 ). To understand this further, we conduct a small-scale qualitative analysis of 10 10 cases where retrieval flips a correct pointwise verdict to an incorrect one (Appendix C.3 ). We only include ideas where the reference judge (no retrieval) is correct in all three aggregated calls and the retrieval judge is incorrect in all three, so the flips are not due to noise. We find that retrieved papers can lead the judge to dismiss contributions it previously considered novel, contrary to the human reviewers and even when nothing in the retrieved work contradicts their novelty. In one case, the judge without retrieval deemed an idea combining two concepts novel, in agreement with the reviewers. Once given papers that present each concept separately, it dismissed the same idea as “a direct combination of existing ingredients…”. Retrieval can also mislead in the opposite direction, overriding the judge’s own knowledge. Without retrieval, the judge correctly described an idea from D − D_{-} as a “broad composition of known components”, but with retrieval it concluded that the idea “…does appear novel in its overall problem formulation and synthesis relative to the provided related work …”. This is especially relevant, since many novelty evaluation pipelines explicitly instruct models to assess ideas against retrieved related work Shahid et al. (2025) ; Moussa et al. (2026) .
blocks.zh: 令人惊讶的是,检索对业绩收益有限,如果有的话(图4)。 为了进一步理解这一点,我们对10个案件进行了小规模的定性分析,其中检索将正确的断点推向错误判断(附录C.3)。 我们只包含所有三个汇总调用中的参考裁判(没有检索)正确,所有三个调用中的检索裁判不正确,所以翻转不是因为噪音. 我们发现,检索到的论文可以让法官驳回它以前认为是新颖的的贡献,这与人类评论员相反,甚至当检索到的作品中没有任何内容与他们的新颖之处相矛盾时。 在一个案件中,未经检索的法官认为,与审查人员一致,将两个新概念结合起来的想法。 一旦得到分别提出每个概念的论文,它便否定了“直接结合现有成分......”的同样想法。 检索也可以误导相反的方向,压倒法官自己的知识。 没有检索,法官正确地将D-D-Q-}提出的一个想法描述为“已知部件的广泛组成”,但通过检索,法官得出结论,“......相对于所提供的相关工作,在总体问题拟订和综合中,......似乎有些新颖......”。 这一点尤其相关,因为许多新颖的评价管道明确指示模型对照检索的相关作品Shahid等人(2025);Moussa等人(2026)。

blocks.en: A possible explanation is that our retrieval pipeline is simply too weak: with a stronger retriever, or more retrieval results, judges would ground their verdicts in the right prior work and the gains would materialize. We test this by replacing the pipeline with a substantially stronger retrieval-augmented judge and asking whether the extra retrieval quality converts into higher performance.
blocks.zh: 一个可能的解释是,我们的检索管道太薄弱:如果检索器更强大,或获得更多的检索结果,法官们就会在正确的先前工作的基础上作出判断,而收益将会实现。 我们通过更换管道来测试这一点,换成一个更强大的检索强化法官,并询问额外检索质量是否转化为更高的性能。

blocks.en: We instantiate a strong agentic RAG judge on top of gpt-5.6-sol , a newer and stronger backbone than any judge considered so far, run at reasoning_effort=xhigh and equipped with a web-search tool. Given an idea, the judge iteratively searches the literature as it sees fit, with no cap on how many searches it issues or how many results it inspects before committing to a verdict. This differs from the pipeline described in § 4 , where judges are handed a fixed set of five pre-retrieved abstracts. We do limit the strong judge to prevent contamination: search is restricted to arxiv.org , and the prompt instructs the judge to consider only papers published before the retrieval cutoff (2025-03-01) and to disregard any hit that is the idea’s own preprint, mirroring a reviewer who stumbles upon the paper under review. Because this judge is costly, we call it once per idea, without verdict aggregation. Appendix B.2 gives the full implementation details.
blocks.zh: 在Gpt-5.6-sol的顶端, 一个比目前任何法官都更新、更强大的骨干, 鉴于一个想法,法官反复搜索其认为合适的文献,没有规定在做出判决之前要进行多少搜索或检查多少结果。 这与第4节所述的管道不同,该节中向法官交付了一套固定的五份预取摘要。 我们确实限制强法官防止污染:搜索仅限于arxiv.org, 及时指示法官只考虑检索截止前(2025-03-01)发表的论文, 因为这位法官费用昂贵, 我们称之为每个想法一次, 没有判决汇总。 附录B.2提供了全面执行的细节。

blocks.en: Figure 5: Stronger retrieval does not help. Pointwise macro-F1 on Human+Generated , for a strong agentic RAG judge ( gpt-5.6-sol with live, iterative web search) against judges using the standard retrieval setup (§ 4 ), which see five pre-retrieved abstracts. All judges run once per idea, without verdict aggregation. Despite a newer backbone, higher reasoning effort, and unlimited search, the agentic judge shows no significant gains.
blocks.zh: 图5:加强检索无济于事。 Pointwise macro-F1 on Human+Generated ),指一名强大的代理RAG法官(gpt-5.6-sol带有直播,迭代网络搜索功能),使用标准检索设置(§4)来对抗法官,参见5份预检索摘要. 所有法官每个想法运行一次,没有判决汇总。 尽管有了较新的骨干,更高的推理努力,以及无限的搜索,代理裁判显示没有重大收益.

blocks.en: Figure 6: Cost vs. pointwise macro-F1 for claude-opus-4-6 , comparing prompted-judge configurations against the dedicated novelty judges, in the Human-Only ( left ) and Human+Generated ( right ) settings (error bars: 95% CIs from a paired bootstrap with 10,000 10{,}000 resamples). blocks.en: All judges so far have been prompted judges: a vanilla LLM, a prompt, and at most a fixed set of retrieved abstracts. blocks.en: Conclusions
blocks.zh: 结论

blocks.en: We ran a controlled study of automated novelty evaluation, sweeping the design choices a practitioner makes when building an LLM novelty judge. To enable this, we devised an automatic pipeline that mines novelty labels from free-text peer reviews and pairs human-authored with LLM-generated ideas, evaluating judges across both distributions.
blocks.zh: 我们对自动化新颖性评价进行了有控制的研究, 研究了从业者在建立LLM新颖性法官时所作的设计选择。 为了能够做到这一点,我们设计了一个自动管道,从自由文本同行评审中取出地雷的新标签,并配以人文作者的LLM产生的想法,评价两种分布的法官。

blocks.en: Judges turn out to be highly sensitive: small edits to the judge prompt swing pairwise accuracy by more than 50 50 points, the same edit helps one backbone and sinks another below chance, and the fixes practitioners reach for first, retrieval and higher reasoning effort, buy little. Paying more does not help either: the dedicated novelty judges we tested are outscored by our cheapest prompted configuration, which operates at a fraction of their cost.
blocks.zh: 法官们变得非常敏感:小编辑给法官的精确度迅速回转50分以上,同样的编辑帮助了一个骨干,另一个在机会以下的下沉,而修补从业者到达的第一,检索和更高的推理努力,买的很少。 支付更多也无济于事:我们所测试的敬业新颖法官被我们最廉价的诱导配置所超越,这种配置以成本的一小部分运作。

blocks.en: Pairwise judges in particular prove least stable in precisely the scenarios they are built to address. Changes that barely move Human-Only performance shift Human+Generated by tens of points, and judges show increased uncertainty once generated data is evaluated. Validating a judge on human-authored papers, or against a single ideation system, says little about how it will behave on the generated ideas it is actually asked to score. Until evaluation protocols account for these sensitivities, automated novelty assessments should be interpreted with significant caution.

blocks.en: We ran a small blind study to check that the weak-labeling assumption behind Human+Generated (Section 3.1 ) is not obviously violated. We conduct retrieval for each benchmark idea by first extracting up to three main contributions using claude-opus-4-6 with the prompt specified in Prompt 14 . blocks.en: We test the significance of every change reported relative to the reference configuration (Section 4.1 ) with a two-sided paired non-parametric bootstrap of 100,000 100{,}000 resamples. For a given judge and metric, we resample the evaluation instances with replacement, apply the same resampled indices to the predictions of the reference and of the modified configuration, and recompute the difference between the two. The bootstrap is corpus-level: on each resample we recompute the metric (macro-F1, soft-accuracy, or strict-accuracy) over the full resampled set. From the resulting distribution of differences we build a bias-corrected and accelerated (BCa) 95 % 95\% confidence interval, and mark a difference with * when this interval excludes zero (i.e., p < 0.05 p<0.05 ).
blocks.zh: 我们测试每一次报告的变化相对于参考配置(第4.1节)的意义,其双侧对齐的非参数靴套为10万个100{,}000个复标。 对于给定的判断和度量,我们用替换来重现评价实例,对参考和修改的配置的预测采用相同的重印指数,并重新计算两者的差异. 靴子是实体级的:在每次重印时,我们都会在重印的全重印上重刻度量表(宏-F1,软精确度,或严格精确度). 通过由此产生的差异分布,我们构建了一个偏差校正和加速(BCa) 95% 95%的置信间隔,并在该间隔排除0时与*(即p < 0.05 p < 0.05)标记差异。

blocks.en: To understand why retrieval (counterintuitively) yields limited gains (Section 5.1 ), we inspect cases where it turns a correct verdict incorrect. We focus on one strong judge, gpt-5.4 , on pointwise Human+Generated , where retrieval flips 22 of its correct verdicts to incorrect. Since each verdict aggregates three calls, a flip in the aggregated verdict could reflect sampling noise rather than an effect of retrieval. We therefore only consider ideas where the reference judge (no retrieval) is correct in all three calls and the retrieval judge is incorrect in all three. We sample five flips per class ( 5 5 from D + D_{+} and 5 5 from D − D_{-} the reference judge classifies correctly). For each, we compare the judge’s reasoning with and without retrieval. We observe a few recurring patterns (see examples for each in Table 7 ).
blocks.zh: 为了了解为什么检索(直觉地)产生有限的收益(第5.1节),我们检查了错误判决的案件。 我们的焦点是一位强势的法官,Gpt-5.4, 对尖端的Human+Generated, 由于每项判决总共三次通话,合并判决的翻转可以反映抽样噪音而不是检索的效果. 因此,我们只考虑在所有三个电话的参考法官(没有检索)正确和检索法官在所有三个电话中不正确的情况下。 我们抽取了每个班的5个翻转(5个来自D + D + + + + + + + + 5个来自D → D + + + + + + + ) 参考法官的分类正确. 对每个法官,我们都要将法官的推理与没有检索的推理进行比较。 我们注意到一些反复出现的模式(见表7)。

blocks.en: This pattern underlies the D + D_{+} flips (the reference judge correctly labels an idea novel and the retrieval judge labels it not novel). We observe that when one retrieved paper shares the idea’s headline framing, the judge treats the remaining contribution as incremental, e.g., a larger benchmark as “primarily a scale/resource extension”, or a new failure mode as “mainly a setting shift” (even when this part of the idea is praised by reviewers).
blocks.zh: 这种模式是D+DQQ翻转的基础(参考法官正确标注了一个思想小说,检索法官标注它不是新奇的). 我们注意到,当一份检索到的论文分享该想法的标题框架时,法官将剩余的贡献视为递增性贡献,例如,更大的基准是 " 主要是规模/资源扩展 " ,或新的失败模式是 " 主要是设定的转变 " (即使这部分想法得到审查者的赞扬)。

blocks.en: This pattern underlies the D + D_{+} flips (the reference judge correctly labels an idea novel and the retrieval judge labels it not novel). The retrieval judge maps each component of the idea to a different retrieved paper and concludes that the whole is “a fairly direct synthesis” (even when human reviewers explicitly describe the idea as a novel combination). Notably, without retrieval, the judge often recognizes the same components as known (“The core ingredients are not individually new”) yet still credits their combination as novel.
blocks.zh: 这种模式是D+DQQ翻转的基础(参考法官正确标注了一个思想小说,检索法官标注它不是新奇的). 检索法官将想法的每个组成部分映射到不同的检索文件,并得出结论,整体是“相当直接的合成”(即使人类审查人员明确将想法描述为新颖的组合)。 值得注意的是,没有检索,法官往往承认已知的相同组件 (“核心成分并非个别的新成分”)但依然认为两者的结合是新的。

blocks.en: This pattern underlies the D − D_{-} flips (the reference judge correctly labels a generated idea not novel and the retrieval judge labels it novel). Without retrieval, the judge dismisses the generated ideas as not novel based on its internal knowledge. With retrieval, it checks each idea against the five retrieved papers, finds none that covers it fully, and concludes it is novel (“does not appear in the provided related work”, “None of the cited papers …”). Our retrieval prompt defines novelty “in relation to the provided related work” (Prompt 16 ), which likely encourages this over-reliance on retrieved papers.
blocks.zh: 这种模式是D-D-QQ-}翻转的基础(参考法官正确地标注了一个生成的想法,而不是新颖的,检索法官标注它的新颖的)。 没有检索,法官基于其内部知识,将所产生的想法视为非新思想。 通过检索,它对照5份检索到的文件检查每个想法,没有找到任何充分涵盖这些想法的文件,并得出结论,这是新颖的(“没有出现在所提供的相关作品中”,“没有一份被引用的论文......”)。 我们的检索即时定义了“与所提供的相关工作有关的”新颖性(方案16),这可能鼓励人们过度依赖检索到的文件。

blocks.en: Table 7: Examples of retrieval hurting gpt-5.4 ( Human+Generated , pointwise). In the first row, a single close precursor outweighs the contribution the reviewers valued. In the second, the judge matches each component to a different retrieved paper and dismisses the combination the reviewers called novel. In the third, the retrieved papers override the judge’s own recognition that the idea is a broad composition of known components: since no single retrieved paper covers the idea in full, the judge concludes it is novel.
